ch6-open.title: Video layouts
ch6-open.standfirst: Canvas M lets you choose how everyone's camera tiles sit around your shared canvas. Pick a quiet strip, a docked rail, or a full-screen grid — and pin the one face you want to keep watching. This chapter walks every surface, every toggle, and the gentle rules behind who lands centre stage.

ch4-concept.heading: One canvas, three surfaces
ch4-concept.lead: Your meeting always has a video surface — the way camera tiles are arranged around the drawing canvas. Canvas M ships three: Minimal, Filmstrip, and Gallery. They are mutually exclusive: you are always in exactly one.
ch4-concept.body: The choice is yours alone. It is a per-user preference, not synced to the room, so switching layouts changes only your screen — never anyone else's. The same tiles power every surface: each person shows their live camera when it is on, or their avatar when it is off, with a name label and a muted badge. Switching surfaces never rebuilds presence; it only re-arranges the same faces.
ch4-concept.pull: Your layout is yours. Switching never touches anyone else's screen.

diagram.label: Minimal · Filmstrip · Gallery share one set of tiles
diagram.cap: The same per-person tile renders in all three surfaces — the layout only changes where they sit.

note.html: Your chosen layout is remembered across reloads (saved locally on this device). A new device or browser starts back at Minimal.

ch4-switch.heading: Switch your video layout
steps: Find the Video layout button in the meeting header — the small icon whose glyph changes to match your current surface.
Click it to open the popover menu.
Pick a surface: Minimal, Filmstrip, or Gallery. A check mark sits beside the one in use.
The menu closes and your canvas re-arranges instantly.
ch4-switch.outcome: Your video surface changes for you only. The header button's icon updates to reflect the new mode.
ch4-switch.note: Below the three surfaces sits a separator and a fourth row — Floating presenter — covered later in this chapter. It is an overlay, not a surface, so it has its own check mark you can turn on or off independently.
ch4-switch.figcap: The Video layout popover: three radio surfaces plus the Floating presenter toggle.

ch4-modes.heading: Minimal, Filmstrip, Gallery

tiles.cap: Just the avatar strip along the bottom. The canvas stays as large as possible — the default, and the choice when drawing is the point.
A full-width rail of camera tiles docked to the bottom (~140px tall). The canvas is pushed up, not covered, so it stays clean and usable above the faces.
A full-screen grid of everyone's camera, like Zoom or Meet. Opens over the canvas as a dialog; close it to return.

ch4-modes.useWhen: Reach for Minimal while you sketch, Filmstrip when you want faces visible without leaving the canvas, and Gallery for a faces-first moment — a round of intros, a vote, a discussion where the drawing waits.

legend.text: Title bar — reads Meeting followed by a count of how many people are shown (e.g. Meeting · 6).
Grid / Speaker sub-mode toggle. Grid tiles everyone equally; Speaker promotes one face to a big stage with the rest in a rail below.
Close button (✕ Close), top-right — exits the gallery and drops you back to the Minimal strip.
A camera tile — live video, or the avatar when the camera is off. A green ring marks whoever is speaking.
Tile label — the person's name, a (You) tag on your own tile, a Host badge for the host, and a 🔇 icon when they are muted.
Pin affordance — a quiet pin glyph on the auto-focused tile, or an Unpin chip on a tile you pinned yourself.

ch4-focus.heading: Focus and pinning
ch4-focus.lead: Across Filmstrip, the Gallery speaker stage, and the floating window, Canvas M always highlights one focused person — the presenter of the moment. You never have to set this; it resolves automatically, and you can override it with a pin.
ch4-focus.body: The focus follows a strict order of precedence, highest wins: your pin → the person sharing their screen → the active speaker → the host → the first tile. So if nobody is pinned or sharing, the focus simply follows whoever is talking. To pin, click any tile (in the gallery or filmstrip) — it is promoted to focus and shows an Unpin chip. Click it again, or pin someone else, to release it. Pins are local and ephemeral: they affect only your view and clear on reload. If the person you pinned leaves the room, the focus quietly falls back down the chain.
ch4-focus.pull: Pin = your pick. Screen-share, then speaker, then host fill in when you haven't pinned anyone.

diagram.label: Pin › screen-share › active speaker › host › first
diagram.cap: Focus precedence — the highest rule that matches a present person wins.

note.html: Pinning is per-viewer — there is no way to force a focus for the whole room from here. Each person chooses their own pin. Host moderation (mute, remove, admit) lives in the Participants panel, not in the video layout controls.

ch4-ref.heading: Every layout control
rows: Opens the surface popover; its icon mirrors your current surface.
Avatar strip only — canvas stays maximal. The default.
Bottom rail of camera tiles that pushes the canvas up (~140px).
PiP of the focused person over the canvas; off by default.
Tiles everyone equally inside the gallery.
One big focused tile, the rest in a rail below.
Pin that person as focus; click again to Unpin.
Exits the gallery back to the Minimal strip.
ch4-ref.note: Surface (Minimal/Filmstrip/Gallery) and the Grid/Speaker sub-mode are both per-user preferences and both survive a reload. Pins and the Floating-presenter toggle are per-session and clear on reload.

host.html: None of these controls are host-gated — every participant has the full set. They change only your own view.

ch4-trouble.heading: Video layout gotchas

rows.sym: A tile shows an avatar, not video
rows.cause: That person's camera is off (or hasn't started). Tiles only show live video while a camera is actually publishing.
rows.fix: Nothing to fix — it's expected. Their face appears the moment they turn the camera on.

rows.cause: Self-view is mirrored on purpose — a front camera reads more naturally that way.
rows.fix: This is intended and affects only your local view; others see you un-mirrored.

rows.sym: The face I pinned jumped to someone else
rows.cause: The pinned person left the room, so focus fell back down the chain (screen-share › speaker › host › first).
rows.fix: Click the tile of the person you want and pin them again.

rows.cause: It is hidden in Gallery mode by design, and it never shows your own face when you're the only person.
rows.fix: Switch to Minimal or Filmstrip, and make sure another participant is present.

rows.sym: My layout reset to Minimal on a new device
rows.cause: The preference is saved per-device; a different browser or machine has no saved choice.
rows.fix: Re-pick your surface from the Video layout popover — it'll stick on that device.

rows.sym: The green ring keeps moving between tiles
rows.cause: The ring marks the active speaker, which naturally shifts as people talk.
rows.fix: Pin the person you want fixed in focus to stop the ring driving the stage.

ch4-trouble.note: A camera tile never goes black on a stream error — if a video track fails to attach, the tile quietly falls back to the avatar instead.
